# Churchill Downs Stakes Recaps: The Falls City and The Cardinal Presented by Resolute Racing


## Nov 26, 2026


Juddmonte’s homebred 3-year-old filly Consequent had a pocket inside trip early on and ran down Regaled in deep stretch to win Thursday’s 111th running of the $300,000 Falls City (Grade III) by 1 ¾ lengths in the traditional Thanksgiving Day fixture at Churchill Downs.


Trained by Bob Baffert and ridden by Fravien Prat, Consequent ran 1 1/8 miles over a “sloppy” track in 1:51.61 to remain unbeaten in five starts, collect her second graded stakes win and third stakes victory overall. Previously, she won the $200,000 Seneca Overnight Stakes at Churchill Downs 68 days ago on Sept. 19.


Breaking from post No. 3 in the field of eight fillies and mares, Consequent, who raced without blinkers for the first time, broke well but let last year’s Remington Park Oaks winner So There She Was and two-time Delaware Handicap (GIII) winner Regaled, who recently finish fifth in the $2 million Breeders’ Cup Distaff (GI), take the lead going into the first turn from her outside. Consequent relaxed nicely as So There She Was led through early splits in :24.17 and :49.54. Regaled made the first move and overtook So There She Was into the final turn after six furlongs in 1:14.88. With three-sixteenths of a mile to the finish, Consequent tipped out from the inside and gradually wore down Regaled for the win.


“I think the blinkers off helped her settle today, especially going a longer distance then her previous starts,” Prat said. “She’s undefeated and no matter the circumstances – longer distance, sloppy track, older horses – she always seems to handle it. Now she’s a perfect 5-for-5.”


This was Consequent’s second win against elders this year. In July prior to her start in the Seneca, she beat four older fillies and mares in an allowance optional claiming event over one mile at Ellis Park, which was her first start of the year. Her 2-year-old season concluded with a victory in the $200,000 Starlet (GII) at Los Alamitos Race Course.


Consequent, a daughter of Into Mischief, paid $3.86, $2.58 and $2.34 as the odds-on 4-5 betting favorite. Regaled, ridden by Luis Saez, returned $3.52 and $2.58. It was another 4 ¾ lengths back in third to Yes It Tiz, who paid $3.14 to show under Florent Geroux at 8-1.


The running order was completed by Chasten, Take Charge Omaha, Miss Authentic, Sugar Fish and So There She Was. Anna’s Promise was scratched.


Thursday’s $181,900 first prize jumped her earnings to $524,360.


Consequent was bred in Kentucky and is out of the Uncle Mo mare Cognitive.


Racing at Churchill Downs continues Friday with the popular day-after Thanksgiving card highlighted by the 152nd running of the $700,000 Clark presented by Norton Healthcare (GII) for older horses. The Clark goes as Race 11 of 12 at approximately 5:54 p.m. (all times Eastern). The first race is 1 p.m.


*************************************************************************************************************************


HEREFORAGOODTIME AMBITOUSLY WINS $294,750 CARDINAL ON FRONT-END


LOUISVILLE, Ky. (Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026) – Hereforagoodtime stole Thursday’s 51st running of the $294,750 Cardinal presented by Resolute Racing (Listed) with a gate-to-wire 4 ¾-length victory over She’s Lookin Lucky on Thanksgiving Day at Churchill Downs.


Hereforagoodtime, a 4-year-old filly owned by Travis Boersma’s Flying Dutchman, ran 1 1/8 miles over “good” turf in 1:49.98 to collect the first stakes win of her career. Walter Rodriguez rode the winner for trainer Brendan Walsh.


“It’s been a really good meet and to win this race makes it even better,” Rodriguez said. “She got a really easy lead and had plenty left down the lane.”


Breaking from post position No. 7 in the field of nine fillies and mares, Hereforagoodtime employed ambitious front-running tactics and opened up by as many as 9 ½ lengths after a first quarter mile in :24.28 and the half in :48.34. She was unpressured throughout in a race of her own down the backstretch. Leaving the final turn after six furlongs in 1:13.05, the field was closing into the margin, but Hereforagoodtime kept on down the stretch and safely maintained her advantage for an impressive victory.


“A lot of credit goes to Walter,” Walsh said. “He didn’t have any pressure on the lead and took advantage of it. The one thing about this filly is she’s not going to give up and she’ll definitely stay. Down the backside I could tell she was traveling well and the pace could also be setting up for (Proctor Street) to make her run. Once (Hereforagoodtime) got to the three-eighths pole you could tell they’d really need to make a run to catch her and Walter saved plenty for down the lane.”


The triumph was worth $178,800 and increased her earnings to $762,874. Hereforagoodtime, who was Grade III-placed three times at age 3, boasts a record of 4-3-4 in 16 starts.


Hereforagoodtime returned $2 mutuels of $14.36, $7.66 and $4.90 as the 6-1 second betting choice. She’s Lookin Lucky, ridden by Florent Geroux at odds of 11-1, returned $11.34 and $7.20. Third-place finisher Miwa (GB), under Jose Ortiz, was another half-length back and paid $5.16 to show at 6-1.


The order of finish was completed by Caviar Breakfast, 7-5 favorite Destino d’Oro, Della Pace (GB), Totally Justified, defending race champion Proctor Street and Vive Veuve. Gallant Greta was scratched.


Prior to the Cardinal, Hereforagoodtime won an allowance race on turf at Keeneland by a neck on Oct. 22.


Hereforagoodtime, a daughter of Justify out of the Speightstown mare First Hour, was bred in Kentucky by WinStar Farm.
